admission.justification: The choice rejects restoring shared caches and first-view changes merely to recover a historical conversion time; future optimization must justify those distinct regressions and memory costs instead of treating local conversion reuse as approval of the removed design.

alternatives.option: Retain conversion-local scan/split hunks and restore shared parser, memo, index and first-view code to the base.
alternatives.reason: The kept local hunks preserve conversion bytes and deliver a measured gain independently of the regressed shared changes; a separate cut measurement supplied the actual retained result.

alternatives.option: Retain the full wider shared-cache and first-view implementation with the original measured conversion path.
alternatives.reason: First-view and index timings were slower than their controls and the parsed memo failed its admitted memory condition; conversion gain did not justify those regressions.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A separately authorized implementation demonstrates nonregression for the affected first-view/index behavior and satisfies its applicable memory and correctness requirements; the historical conversion number alone is not sufficient. Changes to the first-view composition/memo, index-build or validator parse owners, or to the approved R59/R85 performance and memory requirements, reopen examination of those grounds. A trigger requests that examination; it does not establish measured nonregression, memory compliance or authorization to reverse the chosen cut.

consequences: The 20-second conversion target remains missed; retained gain is not full-packet performance acceptance.
The retained CodeObjects split-lines representation consumes additional memory alongside raw blobs; final-cut peak/RSS and incremental cache cost are unmeasured.
Removed parsed-store, process-memo, standby, prewarm and index changes are not supplied by the surviving conversion-local helpers.
context: A wider performance implementation improved cold conversion but made first-view and incremental-index controls slower. Its conversion path shared the parser/memo/input readers being removed, so retaining the whole measured path was incompatible with removing the regressions.
